items.headline: Google explains how Duplex now places business calls inside Gemini
points: Google Research published a post on how Duplex, its calling technology, now calls businesses for users within Gemini.
explainx.ai says these calls are made through Gemini's Tasks feature.
FourWeekMBA notes Duplex first appeared eight years ago.
items.for_you: Gemini users can have it call businesses on their behalf.

items.headline: Gemini app can now turn a text prompt into a GIF
points: Gemini now generates GIFs from a written prompt, Neowin, AndroidPure and Wisevoter report.
Reports differ on access: Neowin says free users get it, AndroidPure says it needs a Google AI plan.
Neowin notes ChatGPT already offers AI-generated GIFs.
items.for_you: Gemini app users can make GIFs, though reports disagree on whether a paid plan is required.

items.headline: Google adds policies that check AI agent actions before they run
points: Google introduced Semantic governance policies, which check what an AI agent is about to do before it does it.
The feature was announced on the Google for Developers blog.
items.for_you: Developers building agents with Google's tools can have planned agent actions checked before they execute.

sources.title: Check what your AI agents do before they do it, with Semantic governance policies

items.headline: Google DeepMind hires Hume AI's chief executive and engineers
points: Google DeepMind has hired Hume AI's CEO along with engineers from the company, Wisevoter reports.
The Economic Times says he is a psychology PhD who taught AI to hear when people are sad, stressed or happy.
The Economic Times says DeepMind wants to bring that ability to Gemini.

items.headline: WhatsApp fixes three security flaws, one suspected in scams
points: WhatsApp has fixed three security flaws, Business Upturn and The 420.in report.
CyberSecurityNews says the Android flaws could let attackers delete users' files and expose IP addresses.
One of the Android bugs is suspected of being used in a scam campaign.
items.for_you: If you use WhatsApp on Android, install the latest app update.

items.headline: Reports say Meta's Muse agent could read Signal chats
points: eSecurity Planet reports Meta's Muse AI agent read Signal messages through Android and Mac permissions.
Awani International lists it among early safety mishaps for Muse; today's items include no response from Meta.
Separately, Signal now blocks AI agents from reading its chats by default, The Register reports.
items.for_you: If you use Muse on Android or Mac, check which apps it has permission to see.

Startup Fortune puts the buildout at $300 billion and the final raise at $20 billion.
CryptoRank reports Oracle says the build no longer depends on extra vendor deals.

items.headline: University of California signs systemwide ChatGPT deal for all students
points: The University of California signed a deal with OpenAI giving all students free ChatGPT access, the Los Angeles Times and EdSource report.
The Sacramento Bee and Superpower Daily put the cost at $1.2 million a year.
Faculty objected, calling the deal 'unwise' and urging a delay, according to EdSource and Superpower Daily.

items.headline: OpenAI's GPT-Live-1.1 voice model cuts idle cost for developers
points: MarkTechPost reports OpenAI has released GPT-Live-1.1 for voice agents, with idle time charged at $0.02 a minute.
This is the second independent report; The Defiant first described the API release with cheaper standby.

items.headline: OpenAI now requires resellers of its models to get approval
points: Companies reselling OpenAI's models must now get OpenAI's approval first, PPC Land reports.
Semafor first reported the tighter reseller rules a day earlier; PPC Land is the second outlet to report them.
items.for_you: Platforms that offer OpenAI models to their own customers may need OpenAI's sign-off.
